inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report, cash-flow note 2.23 share-based payment add-back GBP3.2m; no equity-award tax line (UK net-settlement taxes immaterial, EquityAwardTaxes kpi = 0 every year)
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts GBP/share to pence/share; no market rate involved, no parity check needed. NAV/share GBP39.17 = 3,917p ties to the company's own pence disclosure.
inputs.share_count_basis: 92.9m shares in issue net of treasury (8.106m) and EBT at 30 April 2026 (AR p.~45 'Shares, net of treasury and EBT'), plus 0.2m dilutive share-scheme awards (diluted 96.2m vs basic 96.0m weighted, note 2.7) = 93.1m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so buybacks are value-neutral here. Memo: GBP60m of buybacks May-Aug 2026 (AGM statement 11 Sep 2026) have since retired ~1.6m shares and net cash is guided to ~GBP250m at the half year -- both anchors move together and are left on the 30 April 2026 balance-sheet basis for consistency.
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP-denominated build. UK 10y gilt ~4.5% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.1 (UK housebuilders) = cost of equity ~10.5%; debt is GBP400m 2.5% Green Bond (Aug 2031) + GBP260m Green term loan, after-tax ~3%, but the group is net cash so the capital structure is effectively all-equity with a modest gross-debt offset: WACC 9.5%. Same rate in all three scenarios -- cyclicality is charged in the driver paths and the weights, not stacked on the discount rate (adaptations (f)).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: lease liabilities (GBP4.0m total, note 2.11) are excluded from net debt and the full cash lease charge (GBP2.3m principal + GBP0.2m interest in FY2026 = 0.1% of revenue) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path. Immaterial either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; JV share of results (GBP3.0m FY2026) is left out of the flows and the GBP~190m JV investments carried at book are left out of the bridge -- both are immaterial and offset.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical') with the adaptations file applied: GBP WACC, single lease treatment, SBC near-zero. Berkeley is an inventory-heavy developer but a going-concern operator with 50 years of trading, a replenished land bank and a stated 10-year cash framework, so the owner-FCF route is used rather than the NTA/P-B blend for pure land subdividers; NAV/share (3,917p) is reported as a cross-check, not a value basis. MID-CYCLE DISCIPLINE: FY2026 is the trough of a three-year profit decline (PBT GBP604m FY23 -> GBP451m FY26; EBITDA margin 18.9% vs 20.2% five-year average and 23.3% ten-year average). The base year for the flows is NOT FY2026: the component build starts at the FY2027 guidance level (PBT 'similar to FY2026', so ~19% margin on slightly lower revenue) and ramps the margin to a 21% mid-cycle level by FY2030 -- below the FY2017-19 27-29% peak (pre-RPDT, pre-Building Safety Levy) and at the midpoint of the FY2022-FY2025 range -- and holds it there. Revenue recovers from a sub-FY2019 level only at 3-5% p.a. FY2028-30, then 2.5-3%: FY2036 revenue GBP3.15bn vs GBP2.96bn in FY2019, i.e. modest real growth over 17 years. LAND/WIP REINVESTMENT: for a developer the real 'capex' is land and work-in-progress held in inventory, not PP&E (nil in FY2026). Historically cash generated from operations converts 86% of EBITDA over ten years and 75% over the last five, i.e. 3-5% of revenue is reinvested in inventory each year on average; capex_pct_path carries that as 3.0% of revenue in the base (PP&E ~0.1% + net land replenishment), and wc_capture_pct of -25% charges WIP build on incremental revenue (growth consumes cash for a developer). BTR PLATFORM: the GBP69.2m FY2026 'Additions to investment property' is growth investment in Berkeley Living (GBP1.2bn over 10 years) that builds a yielding asset at cost ~ fair value (note 2.9: 'fair value approximates cost'); it is treated as value-neutral and excluded from both the flows and the bridge rather than charged as capex with no income credited. FY2022 OCF (-GBP129.5m) is distorted by the GBP540.6m net cash movement on the St William 50% asset acquisition (FY22 AR 'Net cash movements on St William asset acquisition') -- non-recurring, excluded from any base. OWNER FCF ANCHOR: reported FCF GBP191.1m (OCF 260.3 - BTR additions 69.2) less SBC 3.2 less finance income 40.8 = GBP147.1m is the contract figure; on the unlevered, ex-BTR basis the engine projects (add back BTR 69.2 and interest paid 27.5) FY2026 was ~GBP244m, and the year-1 component build lands at ~GBP235m -- consistent with a trough year, not a windfall. Interest income (GBP40.8m) is stripped because net cash (GBP363m) is ~1.5x the owner-FCF base and is added back in the bridge. TAX: UK corporation tax 25% + Residential Property Developer Tax 4% = 29% statutory; FY2026 P&L rate 29.5%, cash rate 21.8% (timing); cash tax path 28%. SBC-near-zero market: house and street coincide to within ~0.3% of revenue; band_position is reported but is not economically meaningful here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_3yr_cagr -- book value compounded ~3% p.a. through the downcycle while returning GBP1.0bn to shareholders; used as the long-run (post-recovery) nominal growth anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (+3%) diverges from EPS (-8% 3yr) and owner-FCF (-21% 3yr) CAGRs by more than 30pp: the FCF endpoints are FY2023 (recent cycle peak) to FY2026 (trough), so the trailing CAGRs measure the downcycle, not the trend. Base-case growth is therefore built from mid-cycle recovery judgment, not from the trailing CAGRs.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2021 316.9, FY2023 302.9, FY2026 147.1. The owner-FCF CAGR is below the reported-FCF CAGR by ~4pp mainly because finance income rose from GBP3m to GBP41m on higher rates -- i.e. an increasing share of reported cash flow is interest on the cash pile, not operations. FY2022 excluded as an endpoint (St William acquisition distortion).

base.narrative: FY2027 at guidance (PBT similar to FY2026, revenue ~-2%), then a gradual London/SE recovery as rates ease and forward-sales cover rebuilds; margin recovers to the 21% mid-cycle level by FY2030 with the Building Safety Levy absorbed; land replenished at 3% of revenue; terminal 2% with a 13x cap (cyclical).

bull.narrative: SDLT reform and/or Building Safety Levy relief plus lower mortgage rates unlock the London undersupply backlog; volumes recover faster, margin returns toward the ten-year 23% average on operating leverage; replanning (Southall, Woodberry Down) supplies land without new capital so reinvestment runs at 2.5% of revenue.

bear.narrative: Prolonged London stagnation: higher-for-longer rates, SDLT surcharges and weaker international demand keep forward sales shrinking; Building Safety Levy and RPDT embed permanently and margin settles at 17.5%; 8+ year planning cycles and Gateway 2/3 delays tie more capital in WIP (4% reinvestment); no recovery in volumes beyond inflation.

scenario_narratives.base: The downcycle bottoms in FY2027 at the guided ~GBP450m PBT and recovers gradually rather than sharply. Axes: (1) UK mortgage rates and London affordability, which drive the forward-sales book (GBP1.4bn -> GBP1.0bn in FY2026) and hence FY2028-30 completions; (2) the regulatory cost stack -- RPDT 4%, Building Safety Levy from autumn 2026, Section 106 -- which caps margin recovery at ~21% rather than the 27-29% of FY2017-19; (3) land replenishment largely by replanning existing holdings, keeping reinvestment at ~3% of revenue; (4) Berkeley Living BTR treated as value-neutral (built at cost ~ fair value). Terminal value capped at 13x owner FCF because housebuilding is cyclical.
scenario_narratives.bull: Policy reform (SDLT cut, Building Safety Levy scrapped or sunset, faster Building Safety Regulator approvals) coincides with lower rates, and the structural London/SE undersupply (London delivering <10% of its target) converts into a multi-year volume recovery; Berkeley's brand (NPS +78) and net-cash balance sheet let it lead the upcycle. Margin returns toward the ten-year 23% average on volume leverage and replanning uplift; reinvestment needs fall to 2.5% because density gains supply land without new capital.
scenario_narratives.bear: No policy relief and a prolonged London stagnation: international buyer demand stays weak, rates stay elevated, forward sales keep falling and FY2027-28 revenue drops a further 8% cumulatively with no volume recovery thereafter. The Building Safety Levy and RPDT become permanent, margin settles at 17.5%, and longer planning/Gateway timelines tie up more WIP. The balance sheet (net cash, GBP1.4bn facilities) means this is a value-erosion case, not a solvency case: the bear case still produces positive owner FCF every year.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because three consecutive years of falling profit, shrinking forward sales and a Building Safety Levy landing this autumn make a prolonged-stagnation path a live outcome, not a tail; bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things (UK policy reform and lower rates) to go right together. Net cash and GBP1.4bn of facilities keep solvency out of the bear case, which is why bear is not higher still.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Berkeley on mid-cycle owner cash flow -- neither the FY2017-19 peak margins nor the FY2026 trough -- discounted at a GBP cost of capital, with cyclicality charged once through the scenario paths and weights rather than a WACC premium. Land and WIP reinvestment is the developer's real capex and is charged explicitly; BTR platform investment is treated as value-neutral; interest on the cash pile is stripped from the flows and the cash is added back in the bridge. The published NAV/share (3,917p at 30 April 2026) is a cross-check: the base DCF should sit modestly above book because the land bank is held at cost with GBP6.4bn of estimated future gross margin embedded.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin assumption (21%) may be too high if the Building Safety Levy, RPDT and Section 106 costs are permanent and the FY2017-19 margin regime never returns
Reinvestment at 3% of revenue may understate the cash needed to replenish a GBP5.1bn inventory if replanning stalls and new land must be bought at market
London/SE concentration: a single regional market's rates, SDLT and international-buyer dynamics drive the whole forward-sales book
Berkeley Living BTR is assumed value-neutral; if the GBP1.2bn platform earns below the cost of capital it is a value transfer out of the for-sale business
Balance-sheet anchors are at 30 April 2026; GBP60m of buybacks since and the ~GBP250m half-year net-cash guide move both the share count and net cash together
Terminal value is ~half of enterprise value even with a 13x cap; a lower cap (11x) is the bear case
